title: Stay in the Green Zone
goal: Remain below four meat meals per week.
whyItMatters: Flexitarian diets can significantly reduce climate impacts.

title: Plant Protein Majority
goal: Obtain most protein-containing meals from non-meat protein sources.
whyItMatters: Plant proteins generally require fewer resources than meat production.

title: Legume Champion
goal: Eat legumes in at least five meals.
whyItMatters: Legumes are healthy and environmentally efficient protein sources.

title: Alternative Staples Habit
goal: Include alternative staple foods in at least five meals.
whyItMatters: Alternative crops help reduce dependence on wheat, rice and maize.

title: Sustainable Plate Builder
goal: Create ten meals that combine vegetables, sustainable proteins and sustainable staples.
whyItMatters: Sustainable diets are built around diverse plant-based foods.

title: Beyond Country of Origin
goal: When selecting products for at least 3 meals, consider both country of origin and one additional sustainability indicator (e.g., certification, production method, seasonality).
whyItMatters: Food sustainability depends on multiple factors, not only transport distance.

title: Certification Critic
goal: Choose one product carrying at least two different sustainability labels and record what each label represents.
whyItMatters: Different labels communicate different aspects of sustainability.

title: Multi-Impact Shopper
goal: For at least 3 purchasing decisions, consider two different environmental dimensions before selecting a product.Examples:Land use + carbon footprintCarbon footprint + travel distanceWater use + production method
whyItMatters: Food sustainability is multidimensional.

title: Seasonal Decision Maker
goal: Include seasonal products in at least 4 meals and think of one reason why they were selected.
whyItMatters: Seasonality influences transportation, storage and energy requirements.

title: Informed Purchase Habit
goal: Before purchasing a food product, consider at least three of the following aspects:Country of originProduction methodCertificationSeasonalityTravel distanceApply this process for at least 4 food choices.
whyItMatters: No single environmental indicator is sufficient to determine sustainability.

title: Multi-Criteria Decisions
goal: For at least three purchases, consider both NOVA classification and Green-Score before making a decision. Use Open Food Facts or packaging information.
whyItMatters: Environmental impacts, nutritional quality and processing level do not always align.

title: Three-Indicator Evaluation
goal: For three foods, compare NOVA classification, Nutri-Score and Green-Score whenever all three are available. Use packaging and Open Food Facts.
whyItMatters: : Environmental impacts, nutritional quality and processing level do not always align.

title: Processing Trade-Off Awareness
goal: Identify three foods for which processing appears to create both benefits and drawbacks. Use NOVA classification, ingredient lists and packaging information.
whyItMatters: Processing can improve preservation and convenience while increasing resource use. Food processing has both system benefits and environmental costs.

title: Indicator Diversity Explorer
goal: Track three products representing a wide range of NOVA classifications and Green-Scores and document the differences you observe. Use Open Food Facts and packaging information.
whyItMatters: Processing impacts vary substantially depending on production systems and technologies.

title: Production-Conscious Habit
goal: Use at least one production-related indicator as part of five purchasing decisions. Use packaging, NOVA classification, Green-Score or Open Food Facts.
whyItMatters: Long-term sustainability awareness requires integrating production information into routine decisions.

title: Multi-Criteria Packaging Decisions
goal: For at least three purchases, consider both packaging material and end-of-life options before making a choice. Look at material composition, recycling instructions and reuse information.
whyItMatters: Choosing the most sustainable packaging requires considering the full life cycle.

title: Reuse Habit Builder
goal: Use reusable or refillable packaging systems on at least five occasions.Look for products sold through deposit-return or refill systems.
whyItMatters: Reusable packaging only becomes environmentally beneficial through repeated use. Reusable packaging must reach a break-even point before outperforming single-use packaging.

title: Packaging Trade-Off Observer
goal: Reflect on packaging trade-offs for at least five products. Observe packaging size, materials and protective functions.
whyItMatters: Less packaging is not always the most sustainable choice. Packaging that prevents food spoilage can provide greater environmental benefits than eliminating packaging altogether.

title: Smart Packaging Explorer
goal: Identify packaging innovations on at least two products. Look for freshness indicators, QR codes, traceability features or temperature-monitoring systems.
whyItMatters: Packaging technologies are evolving beyond basic containment. Active and intelligent packaging can help reduce spoilage and improve information sharing.

title: Packaging-Conscious Habit
goal: Use packaging considerations as one of your decision criteria for at least five food purchases. Use packaging labels, recycling instructions and reuse information.
whyItMatters: Consumers influence packaging demand through purchasing choices.

title: Zero Plate Waste Focus
goal: Log at least 7 Half Plate Saved actions. How to do it: Always begin with a smaller serving and only take additional food if required.
whyItMatters: Plate waste prevention starts before food reaches the plate.Smaller servings are associated with lower plate waste.

title: Leftover Economy Expert
goal: Log at least 7 Full Plate Saved actions. How to do it: Store and consume leftover food instead of discarding it.
whyItMatters: Leftover reuse saves food, money and resources.

title: Expiry Prevention Expert
goal: Log 4 Expired Product Consumed actions. How to do it: Prioritise foods approaching their best-before date during the week.
whyItMatters: Premature disposal remains a major source of avoidable waste.

title: First-In, First-Out Expert
goal: Throughout the week, organize your fridge, freezer or pantry so that foods with the shortest remaining shelf life are always placed at the front and used first. Whenever you purchase new food, place older products in front of newer products.
whyItMatters: Many foods become waste simply because consumers forget they already have them.

title: Zero-Waste Planning Week
goal: Plan all main meals for the week before your first shopping trip and only purchase foods that have a planned use. Review your fridge, freezer and pantry before shopping.
whyItMatters: Overbuying and inadequate planning are among the most common causes of household food waste.

title: Rainbow Week
goal: Consume foods from at least five different fruit and vegetable colours every day. Aim to include a mix of green, red, orange, yellow, purple or white fruits and vegetables throughout the day.
whyItMatters: Colour diversity often reflects nutrient diversity.

title: High-Fibre Breakfast Week
goal: Start every day with a breakfast containing a meaningful source of fibre.Build breakfast around oats, whole grains, fruit, seeds, nuts or other fibre-rich foods.
whyItMatters: Breakfast is often one of the lowest-fibre meals of the day.

title: Added Sugar Awareness Week
goal: Avoid foods or drinks with added sugars as one of the first three ingredients throughout the week. Read ingredient lists before consuming packaged foods.
whyItMatters: Many processed foods contain substantial amounts of added sugar.

title: Nutrient-Dense Plate Week
goal: Ensure that every main meal includes at least three of the following: a protein source, a fibre-rich food, a fruit or vegetable, or a source of healthy fats.
whyItMatters: Healthy eating patterns depend on overall nutritional quality.

title: Micronutrient Diversity Week
goal: Consume at least 20 different plant foods throughout the week. Count different fruits, vegetables, pulses, herbs, nuts, seeds and whole grains.
whyItMatters: Dietary diversity improves exposure to vitamins, minerals and beneficial plant compounds.

title: Learn to Log Your Food
goal: Log at least one meal per day
whyItMatters: Understanding your current food habits is the first step towards improving them.

title: Count Your Meat Meals
goal: Track all meat-containing meals.
whyItMatters: Many people are unaware of how frequently meat appears in their diet.

title: Reduce One Meat Meal
goal: Eat one fewer meat meal than during your previous week.
whyItMatters: Small changes are often easier to maintain than drastic dietary changes.

title: First Sustainable Swap
goal: Log 2 protein swap actions. Use any of the available swaps: Beef → Pork, Beef → Chicken, Beef → Legumes, Pork → Chicken, Pork → Legumes or Chicken → Legumes.
whyItMatters: Small substitutions can significantly reduce the environmental impact of meals without requiring major dietary changes.

title: Beef Reduction Starter
goal: Log 2 Beef → Chicken or Beef → Legumes swaps. Whenever you would normally choose beef, choose chicken or legumes instead and record the swap.
whyItMatters: Beef has one of the highest environmental footprints among commonly consumed foods.

title: Origin Tracker
goal: Look for the country of origin for at least 5 food products consumed during the week.
whyItMatters: Understanding where food comes from is the first step toward understanding its environmental journey. Food transport contributes substantially to food-system greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Seasonal Choices
goal: Log 5 meals that include at least one seasonal fruit or vegetable.
whyItMatters: Seasonal foods may reduce storage and transportation needs.Choosing seasonal foods can contribute to lower food-related emissions.

title: Certified Choice
goal: Choose and log products carrying sustainability-related certifications on 3 occasions (e.g. organic, fairtrade, protected geographical indications).
whyItMatters: Certifications can provide information about production practices and supply chains.

title: Local Product Explorer
goal: Log 3 meals containing at least one locally produced product.
whyItMatters: Food choices can influence transport requirements and supply chains.

title: Packaging Information Explorer
goal: For at least 5 food products consumed during the week, look for one piece of environmental or sustainability-related information visible on the packaging.Examples may include the country of origin, a certification label, a production claim, or information related to farming practices.
whyItMatters: Many consumers make food choices without looking at the information available on packaging. Learning where to find sustainability-related information is an important first step towards making more informed food choices.

title: Production Method Observer
goal: Look for information about how at least five food products were produced whenever this information is available. Tip: Look at food packaging, Open Food Facts or scan QR codes. Search for information about farming methods, production systems or sustainability programmes.
whyItMatters: Consumers often know what they eat but not how it was produced.

title: NOVA Explorer
goal: Look for the NOVA classification of at least 3 food products. Use Open Food Facts or products that display NOVA information.
whyItMatters: Food processing ranges from minimally processed foods to highly transformed industrial formulations, and processing level influences nutritional, environmental and economic outcomes.

title: Ingredient List Observer
goal: Review the ingredient lists of at last 5 food products consumed this week and look for information related to the level of processing of the product.Read the ingredient list directly on the package. Ultra-processed foods are typically formulated from refined ingredients and additives and are often far removed from their original raw materials.
whyItMatters: Ingredient lists provide clues about the degree of transformation and complexity of food products.

title: Green-Score Awareness
goal: Identify the Green-Score of at least five foods consumed whenever the information is available. Use product labels or Open Food Facts.
whyItMatters: Environmental sustainability is influenced by many stages of food production and processing.

title: First Processing Swap
goal: Log 2 processed foods-related swaps.Eligible actions:Sugary Drink → WaterSugary Snack → Fruit or NutsSugary Cereal → Oats/FruitReady Meal → Home-Cooked MealProcessed Meat → Legumes
whyItMatters: Small substitutions can reduce reliance on highly processed foods while improving nutritional quality and lowering environmental impacts.

title: Packaging Material Observer
goal: Identify the packaging material of at least five food products consumed during the week. Common materials include plastic, glass, paper, cardboard, aluminium and composite materials.
whyItMatters: Different packaging materials have different environmental characteristics and recycling routes.

title: Recycling Label Reader
goal: Check the disposal or recycling instructions on at least ten food packages.Look for recycling symbols, material codes or sorting instructions on the packaging.
whyItMatters: Correct sorting improves recycling quality and material recovery.

title: Packaging Awareness
goal: Reflect on the packaging type of at least 10 foods consumed this week.Observe whether products are sold in glass, plastic, cardboard, metal, composite or refillable packaging.
whyItMatters: Packaging choices influence resource use, recyclability and waste generation.

title: Reusable Packaging Spotter
goal: Identify reusable or refillable food packaging options on at least five occasions. Look for refill symbols, deposit-return systems, refill stations or reusable packaging claims.
whyItMatters: Reusable systems can reduce packaging waste when used repeatedly.

title: Packaging Information Collector
goal: Look for at least one packaging-related characteristic for ten food products consumed. Use information visible on the packaging, such as material type, recycling instructions, recycled-content claims or reuse claims.
whyItMatters: Packaging contains information that consumers often overlook.

title: Smart Serving Starter
goal: Log 5 Half Plate Saved actions. How to complete it: Serve approximately half of what you think you will eat and only take more if you are still hungry.
whyItMatters: People frequently overestimate how much food they need.Smaller initial portions can reduce plate waste and help consumers better match portions to appetite.

title: Leftover Rescuer
goal: Log 3 Full Plate Saved actions. How to complete it: Save unfinished cooked food for a future meal instead of discarding it.
whyItMatters: Leftovers are one of the main sources of avoidable household food waste. Food-management skills such as using leftovers are important drivers of household food waste reduction.

title: Date Label Explorer
goal: Log 1 Expired Product Consumed action. How to complete it: Safely consume foods past their best-before date when appropriate.
whyItMatters: Many edible foods are discarded because consumers misunderstand date labels. Confusion between best-before and use-by dates contributes significantly to avoidable food waste.

title: Storage Smarter
goal: Make sure you read carefully packaging instructions on how to storage food after opening package for at least five products purchased.
whyItMatters: Improper storage causes food to spoil unnecessarily. Inadequate storage is a major driver of consumer food waste.

title: Consistency Builder
goal: Log at least one food-saving action on 4 different days. Use any of the three tracking actions.
whyItMatters: Repeating small actions helps build long-term habits. Food waste is strongly linked to everyday routines and household practices.

title: Protein Every Day
goal: Include a protein-rich food in at least one meal every day. How to do it: Choose foods such as beans, lentils, chickpeas, eggs, fish, dairy products, tofu, tempeh, nuts or seeds and make them a visible part of at least one meal each day.
whyItMatters: Proteins are essential for muscle maintenance, immune function, hormone production and many other physiological processes.

title: Add One More Fruit or Vegetable
goal: Add one extra serving of fruit or vegetables to your diet each day. How to do it: Add fruit to breakfast, include an extra vegetable at lunch, or increase the vegetable portion at dinner.
whyItMatters: Fruits and vegetables provide vitamins, minerals, fibre and antioxidants.

title: Drink Upgrade
goal: Log 3 Sugary Drink → Water swaps.
whyItMatters: Sugar-sweetened beverages are one of the largest contributors to free sugar intake.

title: Whole Grain Week
goal: Choose a whole-grain product every day.How to do itSelect foods such as whole-grain bread, whole-wheat pasta, oats, brown rice, rye bread, quinoa or other whole grains.
whyItMatters: Whole grains provide fibre and other nutrients that are often removed during refining.

title: Smart Snack Swap
goal: Log 5 Snack → Fruit or Nuts swaps.
whyItMatters: Fruit and nuts generally provide more fibre, vitamins and minerals than sugary snack foods.

title: Sustainable Swap Builder
goal: Log 4 protein swap actions. Use any of the available swaps: Beef → Pork, Beef → Chicken, Beef → Legumes, Pork → Chicken, Pork → Legumes or Chicken → Legumes.
whyItMatters: Repeated substitution helps establish more sustainable protein choices.

title: Climb the Protein Ladder
goal: Log at least one swap from each impact level:Beef → Pork or Beef → ChickenBeef → LegumesPork → Legumes or Chicken → LegumesProgressively replace higher-impact proteins with lower-impact options.
whyItMatters: Not all protein substitutions have the same environmental benefit. Moving from beef to legumes generally produces larger environmental savings than moving from beef to pork.

title: Two meat free days
goal: Complete two meat-free days.
whyItMatters: Diets with less meat generally produce fewer greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Legume Routine
goal: Include legumes in four meals.
whyItMatters: Legumes are among the most sustainable protein sources available.Are rich in protein, fibre, vitamins and minerals while having a low environmental footprint.

title: Diversify Your Proteins
goal: Consume four different protein sources.
whyItMatters: Dietary diversity increases resilience and nutritional quality.

title: Diverse Origins
goal: Track the origins of foods consumed and log at least 3 meals with locally produced products.
whyItMatters: Understanding sourcing patterns helps consumers become more aware of food supply chains.

title: Seasonal Week Builder
goal: Include seasonal ingredients in at least 8 meals.
whyItMatters: Seasonality can influence environmental impacts associated with storage and transportation.

title: Certification Habit
goal: Log at least 3 meals including the use of certified products.
whyItMatters: Certification labels can help identify alternative production systems.

title: Product Information Tracker
goal: Record at least two pieces of sustainability-related information for 5 products consumed. Examples: origin or certification.

title: Climate-Conscious Shopping
goal: On five occasions, intentionally select a product after examining environmental information available on the package.
whyItMatters: Purchasing decisions are an important leverage point for food-system sustainability.

title: Production-Informed Choice
goal: Use NOVA classification, Green-Score or ingredient-list information to guide at least five purchasing decisions.Where can I find this information?Use packaging, Open Food Facts or food-scanning applications.
whyItMatters: Production-related information becomes meaningful when it influences choices.

title: Compare Processing Levels
goal: Compare foods with different NOVA classifications on at least three products belonging to the same food category (e.g. three types of cheese). Use NOVA information from Open Food Facts or product labels.
whyItMatters: Foods within the same category may differ substantially in their level of processing.

title: Lower-Processing Action Week
goal: Log 4 processing-related swaps. Eligible actions:Sugary Drink → WaterSugary Snack → Fruit or NutsSugary Cereal → Oats/FruitReady Meal → Home-Cooked MealProcessed Meat → Legumes
whyItMatters: Awareness becomes meaningful when it is translated into concrete food choices.

title: Multiple Indicators Tracker
goal: For four purchased foods, compare NOVA classification with either Green-Score or Nutri-Score.
whyItMatters: Different indicators provide different perspectives on food quality and sustainability.

title: Production and Sustainability Diary
goal: Keep a record of production-related indicators for six foods consumed and reflect on whether they influenced your choices. Use food packaging, NOVA, Green-Score and Open Food Facts.
whyItMatters: Awareness is an important precursor to behavior change.Food-system sustainability depends on decisions made across production, processing and consumption stages.

title: Packaging-Informed Choices
goal: Consider packaging characteristics when making at least three purchasing decisions. Use packaging labels, recycling information and material identification symbols.
whyItMatters: Consumer choices can support packaging systems that use resources more efficiently. Reducing unnecessary packaging is the first priority in the European packaging hierarchy.

title: Recyclability Tracker
goal: Identify whether at least ten food packages appear easy or difficult to recycle based on the information provided.
whyItMatters: Recyclability varies considerably between packaging formats.Packaging that cannot be reused or recycled becomes a lost resource rather than a valuable material.

title: Reuse Opportunity Finder
goal: Choose reusable or refillable packaging options on at least two occasions this week. Look for refill schemes, return systems and reusable packaging labels.
whyItMatters: Reuse systems keep materials in circulation longer. Reuse can reduce demand for virgin materials and packaging waste.

title: Packaging Comparison Diary
goal: Compare packaging materials for three similar food products. Use the information printed on packaging and observe differences in materials.
whyItMatters: The same food category often uses different packaging solutions.

title: Circular Packaging Explorer
goal: Identify packaging that can be reused, recycled or refilled for at least four food products.
whyItMatters: A circular economy depends on keeping materials in use. The European packaging hierarchy prioritises reducing, then reusing, then recycling.

title: Meal Planning Habit
goal: Create a meal plan before one main shopping trip.
whyItMatters: Planning reduces over-purchasing and expiration.

title: Leftovers First
goal: Eat leftovers before preparing a new meal on at least 3 occasions.
whyItMatters: Many leftovers become waste because they remain forgotten. Food-management skills strongly influence household waste levels.

title: Mission 3: Fridge Check Routine
goal: Perform a fridge or pantry check before a main shopping trip.Tracking ComponentLog at least 3 Expired Product Consumed actions or 3 Full Plate Saved actions.
whyItMatters: Consumers often buy products they already have.

title: Portion Control Pro
goal: Log at least Half Plate Saved actions. How to do it: Start every meal with a smaller serving and only add more food if necessary. If you manage to save food with this behavior, log a half plate saved action.
whyItMatters: Over-serving is a common cause of plate waste. Portion size is an important driver of food waste.

title: Leftover Champion
goal: Log at least 3 Full Plate Saved actions. How to do it: store leftover meals or ingredients for future consumption instead of discarding them. If you manage to eat a full meal with leftovers, you can log a full plate saved action.
whyItMatters: Many food items become waste because they are not reused.Using leftovers is an effective strategy to reduce household food waste.

title: Processed Meat Replacement
goal: Log 2 Processed Meat → Legumes swaps.
whyItMatters: Legumes provide protein and fibre while processed meat consumption should be limited for health reasons.

title: Fibre With Every Meal
goal: Include at least one fibre-rich food in every main meal. Use foods such as vegetables, fruits, pulses, nuts, seeds and whole grains as part of breakfast, lunch and dinner.
whyItMatters: Most Europeans consume less fibre than recommended.

title: Salt-Free Table
goal: Do not add salt to food at the table throughout the week. Rely on herbs, spices, garlic, lemon or other flavourings rather than additional table salt.
whyItMatters: Most populations consume substantially more sodium than recommended.

title: Healthy Fat Upgrade
goal: Choose a source of unsaturated fat instead of a source of saturated fat on at least five occasions. Select foods such as olive oil, nuts, seeds, avocados or fish instead of butter, cream, fatty meats or other sources high in saturated fat.
whyItMatters: The quality of dietary fat is important for cardiovascular health

title: Protein Variety
goal: Consume at least four different protein sources during the week. How to do it: Vary protein intake by including combinations of legumes, dairy products, eggs, fish, nuts, seeds, tofu or lean meats.
whyItMatters: Different protein foods provide different nutrients and amino acid profiles.
